dimensions.label: Performance
dimensions.evidence: budgets.cold_start=pass (navigation to booted-with-frames in 882ms (contract <= 3000ms)); jankRate=0.981, p95FrameMs=100
dimensions.rationale: Graded from measured browser evidence (see evidence).

dimensions.label: Visual beauty and cohesion
dimensions.evidence: end.png: rich cloud backdrop, two dark purple hole vortexes clearly visible; census lists shard, shard_cyan, shard_gold on stage yet none are discernible in the screenshot (one gold sliver is clipped at the very bottom edge); black rectangular bar spans the bottom of the play area above the status line.
dimensions.rationale: The painterly sky background is genuinely beautiful — layered warm clouds with real depth — and the two torn holes read instantly as dark vortexes against it. But the hero is small, the collectible shards are not visible anywhere in the frame despite being on stage, and a hard black bar cuts across the bottom of the playfield, breaking the composition and suggesting a clipping/safe-area defect.

dimensions.label: Character design and readability
dimensions.evidence: end.png: demon at top right with visible eyes/brow and spiral body; heroine at lower right on a white cloud holding a staff, rendered small (census player scale 0.38).
dimensions.rationale: The storm-cloud demon is the standout: a dark cloud body with an angry face and a curled spiral tail gives it personality and instant hazard readability. The heroine is a appealing design — figure with staff and flowing ribbons on a cloud — but at scale 0.38 she is small enough that her silhouette and face lose detail at mobile size.

dimensions.label: Animation and game feel
dimensions.evidence: observations.framesRendered = 52; events contain only start, collect, first_reward; milestoneVisuals declares hole/hole2 states for 0.4/0.7 progress but no milestone event occurs in the tail.
dimensions.rationale: Almost no animation evidence exists in this pack: the captured session is 52 frames with a start and a single collect, no milestone, damage, or repair moment was observed, and the declared feedback is only 'juice: standard'. The one thing the fantasy needs — a hole visibly mending — is declared in milestone visuals but never seen in the evidence.

dimensions.label: Plot and emotional arc
dimensions.evidence: intent: 'Ride the cloud, catch falling sky shards, and mend the holes torn in the sky'; end.png shows the two holes in the sky; HUD '★ 1/10'; win title declared 'The sky is mended!'.
dimensions.rationale: The premise — ride the clouds, gather sky shards, mend the holes torn in the sky — is visible in action, not just text: the holes are right there in the sky and the shards are the repair material. Milestones map to hole states, promising a visible arc from torn to mended. The observed session ends at 1/10, so the payoff (a mended sky, win title 'The sky is mended!') is designed but unevidenced.

dimensions.label: Strategy and meaningful choices
dimensions.evidence: experience declares only drag_x controls and a collect objective — no bonk/staff action; failure = health 3 with invulnerableMs 1000; event tail shows one collect and no damage or hazard event.
dimensions.rationale: There is more texture than a pure catcher — 3 health, hazards in the world, a 1-second invulnerability window — so positioning has risk attached. But the review focus's staff/bonk mechanic appears nowhere in the declared controls or objective, so if it exists it is undiscoverable from the design contract; the evidenced play is a single collect with no hazard interaction, leaving the strategic layer mostly theoretical.

dimensions.label: Level and progression design
dimensions.evidence: pacing.targetSessionSec 25, ramp 1 → 1.2 → 1.45, milestones [0.4, 0.7, 1]; observations end at score 1/10 after 52 frames with no milestone reached.
dimensions.rationale: On paper the pacing mirrors a sensible template — 25-second target, three-step speed ramp, milestones at 40%/70%/100% tied to hole repair. But the pack's only session stalls at 1/10 shards with health untouched, so neither the difficulty curve nor the repair progression is demonstrated; the design is plausible but unproven by the evidence provided.

dimensions.label: Audio and feedback
dimensions.evidence: experience.feedback = {haptics: 'none', juice: 'standard'}, no audio fields in the design; events list contains only start/collect/first_reward.
dimensions.rationale: No audio is declared or evidenced: feedback is haptics 'none' plus generic juice, and the event tail has no sound cues for shard collects, damage, or hole repair. In a game built around magical repair moments, the absence of any evidenced collect or mend sound leaves those beats unfelt.

dimensions.label: Originality and coherence
dimensions.evidence: end.png art direction (painterly sky, vortex holes, cloud demon) and intent's sky-mending fantasy; archetype is 'catcher' but theme/mechanic/visuals are uniquely fused.
dimensions.rationale: A ribbon heroine mending a torn sky in a Chinese-fantasy idiom, opposed by a storm-cloud demon, is a distinctive identity — the art direction, premise, and antagonist all pull from the same imaginative source rather than a stock template. Only the underlying catcher chassis is conventional.

dimensions.label: Usability and accessibility
dimensions.evidence: audience: 'family; Chinese-language fantasy adventure' vs end.png strings 'Ribbon Mends the Sky' and 'Gather 10 sky shards' in English; HUD '★ 1/10 ♥ 3' is clear; gold shard clipped at bottom edge of end.png.
dimensions.rationale: HUD is clean — star progress plus heart icons are instantly readable — and controls are a single drag gesture. However: the audience is declared as Chinese-language, yet every visible string (title, objective status) is in English; the hero and shards are small/low-visibility at mobile size; and the black bar at the bottom of the playfield indicates content is being clipped where a shard is visibly cut off at the edge.

improvementSuggestions.problem: The central fantasy beat — a hole in the sky mending — is never evidenced; no repair animation is declared beyond generic juice.
improvementSuggestions.suggestion: When a milestone lands, animate the targeted hole shrinking with light stitching/ribbon threads pulling its edges together over ~0.5s, and add a sparkle trail to falling shards so the repair loop is visible in motion.

improvementSuggestions.problem: A black bar clips the bottom of the playfield and shards on stage are effectively invisible in the frame.
improvementSuggestions.suggestion: Fix the playfield/safe-area sizing so no black bar overlays the world, and give shards a bright rim glow plus slightly larger scale so collectibles read against the bright cloud background at a glance.

improvementSuggestions.problem: Declared audience is Chinese-language but all visible UI text is English, and the small hero/shards strain legibility.
improvementSuggestions.suggestion: Ship the UI strings (title, objective, win/lose) in Chinese for this audience, enlarge the hero modestly, and add a soft outline to the heroine so she separates from bright cloud areas.

improvementSuggestions.problem: The heroine's silhouette and details wash out at scale 0.38 against a bright, busy sky.
improvementSuggestions.suggestion: Increase hero scale slightly and add a subtle drop shadow/outline; keep the demon as-is — it already reads well — and match future hazards to its contrast level.

improvementSuggestions.problem: The staff/bonk interaction in the review focus is absent from the declared controls, so players cannot discover it from the design.
improvementSuggestions.suggestion: Either declare the bonk explicitly (tap while overlapping a demon to bonk it, with a one-line hint on the start card) or remove it from the game's promises; also show a brief shield shimmer during the 1s invulnerability so the health system is legible.

improvementSuggestions.problem: Milestone pacing (0.4/0.7/1) is coarse — long stretches with no visible world change early in a 25s session.
improvementSuggestions.suggestion: Add an early visible change at ~0.2 progress (first hole begins to glow/stitch at its rim) so players see the sky responding well before the first full milestone.

improvementSuggestions.problem: The mending arc is designed but the win payoff is a single text title; the demon has no narrative role beyond decoration.
improvementSuggestions.suggestion: On the win, show both holes fully closed with a light sweep across the sky and the demon cloud dispersing or retreating, so the story resolves visually, and let the demon drift closer as progress stalls to add gentle narrative pressure.

improvementSuggestions.problem: No declared or evidenced sound for collects, damage, or repairs.
improvementSuggestions.suggestion: Add a glassy chime for shard collects, a soft woven 'stitch' sound at hole milestones, and a muted thud plus brief hush on damage; declare them in the feedback design.
